item.text: {"summary":"Draft is mostly coherent, but the resolution date and interval justification need stronger official or empirical support before publication.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"blocking","summary":"The resolver and first-print rule are clear, but the 2026-06-30 resolution date is supported by inferred cadence from the latest February release, not by an official March 2026 release calendar, placeholder, or stated CMS schedule.","actionRequested":"Cite an official CMS release calendar, March 2026 placeholder, or explicit publication policy supporting 2026-06-30; otherwise revise the resolutionDate to the earliest defensible official availability date/rule."},{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The 80% interval is described as wider than recent momentum, but it is not tied to realized forecast errors, monthly volatility over a stated window, or a quantified first-print uncertainty calculation.","actionRequested":"Add a short empirical basis for the +/-810k to +/-840k range, such as recent preliminary monthly change distribution, historical March changes, or prior first-print dispersion."},{"rubricItem":"update","severity":"warning","summary":"The point forecast uses a milder March decline than the recent average because unwinding attrition has normalized, but the cited evidence does not directly quantify why the decline should ease from about -145k to -124k.","actionRequested":"State whether this is a judgmental inside-view adjustment and cite a concrete supporting indicator, or keep the persistence prior closer to the recent average."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Use exact official recent enrollment counts rather than rounded historical context values if available.","Name the exact data.medicaid.gov dataset/table field used for Total Medicaid and CHIP Enrollment to reduce resolver ambiguity."]}
